Iodine: Deﬁciency disorders and prevention programs


palpation. Portable ultrasound equipment can be used in the ﬁeld, and goiter classiﬁed according to international reference criteria
for iodine-sufﬁcient children by age, gender, and body surface area. The total goiter rate is used to deﬁne severity using the following
criteria: <5%, iodine sufﬁciency; 5.0–19.9%, mild deﬁciency; 20.0–29.9%, moderate deﬁciency; and >30%, severe deﬁciency
(World Health Organization et al., 2007).
Because >90% of ingested iodine is excreted in the urine, UI is an excellent indicator of recent iodine intake. Most methods of
measuring UI are based on the Sandell–Kolthoff reaction, in which iodide catalyzes the reduction of yellow ceric ammonium sulfate
to the colorless cerous form, in the presence of arsenious acid. For populations, because it is impractical to collect 24 h samples in
